newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weaker yen pushes Honda profits into overdrive.
newsitem.headline: Weaker yen pushes Honda profits into overdrive.

text.p: Honda Motor Co. Ltd said Tuesday that its profits more than tripled in its latest fiscal year as the weaker yen galvanised overseas sales.

Japan's third largest automaker said its group net profit for the year ended March 31 rose 212 percent to a record 221.17 billion yen ($1.97 billion). The profit surpassed the previous record of 146.5 billion yen ($1.30 billion) in the year ended February 1986.
Group sales also rose 24.5 percent to a record level.

Honda is the first of Japan's auto giants to announce its annual earnings for 1996/97 and the pattern was likely to be repeated by the other big names, which enjoyed a similar windfall from the weaker yen.
Honda's parent current profit also hit a record 166.62 billion yen ($1.48 billion), 3.5 times larger than the year-ago level.

"The increase in revenue was led primarily by higher unit sales of automobiles in Japan and major overseas markets. In addition, the depreciation of the yen positively affected revenue," Honda said in a statement.
It added that profits also benefitted from cost-cutting.
Honda said its group car sales in 1996/97 totalled 2.18 million units, 15.7 percent higher than the previous year. Its automobile business revenue for the year rose 27.7 percent.
"Favorable sales in major automobile markets, in particular newly introduced models in Japan and North America, were primarily responsible for the increase in sales," Honda said.
Honda said it would further increase car sales in the current fiscasl year, especially in North America and Japan.
Honda's group business result includes earnings by Honda and its subsidiaries both in Japan and abroad.
The yen averaged 112.70 yen to the dollar during the last business year, 14.4 percent lower than a year earlier, Honda said.
A weak yen makes Japanese firms' products more competitive in overseas markets and boosts the yen value of sales done in foreign currencies.
A dollar rise by one yen translates into an annual group profit of six billion yen ($53.5 million) for Honda, a spokesman said.
